name: Valentin Borisovich Aleskovskii
summary: Soviet chemist and professor who proposed the framework hypothesis and founded the molecular layering method.

name: Stanislav Ivanovich Kol'tsov
summary: Soviet chemist and graduate student of Aleskovskii who experimentally substantiated the molecular layering method.

name: T. Suntola
summary: Finnish physicist who independently invented atomic layer epitaxy.

name: Anatolii A. Malygin
summary: Russian chemist and student of Aleskovskii who co-authored this historical essay.

name: Victor E. Drozd
summary: Russian physicist and student of Aleskovskii who developed vacuum ML equipment.

name: Riikka Puurunen
summary: Finnish scientist who initiated the Virtual Project on the History of ALD.

name: N. A. Kosygin
summary: Prime Minister of the USSR who became interested in ML research.

name: Leningrad Technological Institute by Lensovet
summary: Technical university in Leningrad/St. Petersburg where the molecular layering method was developed.

name: Leningrad State University
summary: University where Aleskovskii served as rector and founded the Department of Solid State Chemistry.

name: Academy of Sciences of the USSR
summary: Soviet national academy of sciences where Aleskovskii was a corresponding member.

name: Mary
summary: City in Turkmenistan where Aleskovskii was born.

name: Leningrad
summary: City in Russia where Aleskovskii worked and studied.

name: Framework hypothesis
summary: Theoretical concept proposed by Aleskovskii regarding the chemical structure of solids.

name: Molecular Layering
summary: Gas-phase layer by layer deposition technology developed in the Soviet Union.

name: Atomic Layer Epitaxy
summary: Thin-film deposition method patented by Suntola, equivalent to Molecular Layering.

name: Chemical assembly of materials
summary: Inter-university scientific and technical program founded in 1978.
